{{Short description|German physicist and diplomat (born 1961)}}
{{BLP sources|date=September 2016}}

'''Holger G. Ziegeler''' (born June 20, 1961, in [[Regensburg]]) is a German [[physicist]] and [[diplomat]].

He studied [[mathematics]], [[physics]] and [[theoretical linguistics|general linguistics]] at the [[University of Regensburg]], the [[University of Vienna]], and as a [[Fulbright]] scholar at the [[Ohio State University]] in [[Columbus (Ohio)]], obtaining his [[Master of Science]] degree in 1984 and the title of ''Diplom-Physiker'' in 1987.  After initial research in [[particle physics]], he turned to [[artificial intelligence]] ([[artificial neural network|neural networks]], [[knowledge engineering]], [[hypertext]])<ref>[https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Holger-G-Ziegeler-70860494 research publications]</ref> in the course of his work for [[Siemens#Research and development|Siemens Austria]] (1987-1992).

After joining the German [[diplomatic service]] in 1992, Ziegeler held different positions in [[Germany]], [[Paraguay]], the [[United States]], and [[Ethiopia]]. Between 2007 and 2011, he focused on multilateral development policy with the [[World Bank Group]]. He was instrumental in the creation of the [[International Finance Corporation|IFC]] Infrastructure Crisis Facility<ref>[http://ifcext.ifc.org/ifcext/pressroom/ifcpressroom.nsf/1f70cd9a07d692d685256ee1001cdd37/1fac6ade874e5db8852575a8007604a7?OpenDocument World Bank Group Launches Multi-Billion Infrastructure Initiatives to Help Developing Countries Weather Crisis: Germany and France first to join Infrastructure Crisis Facility] - IFC, 25 April 2009</ref> and initiated the [[Politics of Germany#Executive|German Federal Government]]‘s concept on powers shaping [[globalization]].<ref>[https://gestaltungsmaechtekonzept.home.blog Shaping Globalization – Expanding Partnerships – Sharing Responsibility]. Berlin, 2012.</ref>

During 2011 Ziegeler served as Coordinator of the [[International Conference on Afghanistan, Bonn (2011)|International Afghanistan-Conference in Bonn]].

In 2012, he was appointed Director of the [[Embassy of Germany, Washington, D.C.#Consulates and GIC|German Information Center USA]] in [[Washington, D.C.]]  He joined the Federation of German Industries in [[Berlin]] in 2013 as Special Representative for International Economic Partnerships and Alliances and returned in 2014 to the [[Federal Foreign Office]] as Head of International Economic Promotion in Countries and Regions.

In 2016, he was appointed as German [[Consul General]] in [[Jeddah]], [[Saudi Arabia]], and (effective 2018) Special Representative for the [[Organisation of Islamic Cooperation]] (OIC). In July 2020, he received a new commission as Consul General in [[Karachi]], [[Pakistan]],<ref>[https://ibb.co/FsZ5bwX Letter of Commission]{{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> where he served until October 2022 before assuming responsibility for the digitalization strategy and national digitalization policy in the [[Federal Foreign Office|Foreign Office]]. Based on his earlier professional background, he initiated the [[Artificial Intelligence|AI]] Charter (''"KI Charta"'') of the Federal Foreign Office,<ref>[https://www.linkedin.com/posts/holger-ziegeler-0776a559_alecosphere-govtechcampus-foreignsecuritypolicy-activity-7117101095092371456-0Ab5 Consultations between Foreign Office and "AI Ecosphere"]</ref> which published guiding principles for the responsible and effective use of [[Artificial Intelligence|AI]] in February 2025.<ref>[https://www.auswaertiges-amt.de/de/aussenpolitik/sicherheitspolitik/cyber-aussenpolitik/ki-charta-2698666 Das Auswärtige Amt gibt sich eine KI-Charta (de)]</ref> He retired in 2025.
